Finding.Text: The BN case ids are swapped between conformance.md and the suite: conformance.md defines BN-04 as the contract altered after approval and BN-05 as the missing or wrong Bound, while briefless.test.ts titles the missing-Bound test BN-04 and the altered-contract test BN-05, and test-titles.txt mirrors the swap. Both behaviours are exercised with restoring controls, so the gates are covered; the registry and the suite disagree on which case is which. In addition, BN-05's "or carries a wrong definition hash" variant has no test: every Bound-failure test omits a Bound (the briefless unbound test and RV-09), so rule 7's wrong-hash branch in state.ts ("Bound of check ... is not the hash of its definition") is unexercised and A4's "a missing or wrong Bound still fails" rests on the shared predicate rather than on a test of the wrong-hash case. Fix: swap the two test titles and their test-titles.txt lines to match conformance.md, and add one Bound carrying a wrong definition hash to the briefless unbound test.

K7 orders this change to execute only after all seven prepared changes close, or after their own approved material revisions remove the protection. The start run run-1 began 2026-11-17T07:57:19Z while C-0018-deduplicated-packages, the last of the seven, was still open; it closed at 08:22:24Z with its templates/** and brief.md protection intact (revision 2 did not remove it). The baseline start run therefore preceded the last close by about 25 minutes, a literal deviation from the sequencing clause. No source was written and no protected document deleted before the last close: the implementation commit 41f910a (08:44:30Z) and the source-identity revert 81b5349 (08:45:17Z) both follow every close, and C-0018's final evidence (run-3, 08:05 to 08:08Z) ran while brief.md still existed, so the constraint's protective purpose held and no evidence of either change was compromised. The start revision is retained by design and a second start run is refused, so the timing cannot be repaired without rewriting history; recorded non-blocking for the owner's sequencing ruling.

A pass separates a kernel that compiles — the optional briefSha256 and brief fields, the legacyBrief gate, the rule-3 exemption and the changed tests included — from one with a type error, which is A8's first clause. It runs no behaviour: a gate that still demands a brief for a new approval, or one that no longer refuses a mismatched legacy brief, type-checks as well as the correct one; those rest on CK2, CK6 and the diff read. Claim is command-completion only.

bun test --parallel reports 129 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, 1680 expect calls across 17 files (run-3 log), against the run-1 baseline of 123 pass, 1 skip, 1627 expects across 16 files on the same start tree: exactly the five BN cases and CL-06 added, one new file (briefless.test.ts), and the single skip is the pre-existing win32-conditional case also skipped at start. The suite exercises failure paths with controls, not just the happy path: BN-03 refuses close on an edited and on a missing legacy brief and closes once the original page is restored; the unbound approval is a check defect and holds start; the altered contract is reported altered after approval and refuses close until the approved bytes return; FS-12, FS-14, RV-04 and RV-10 keep the legacy refusal paths; FL-04 shows an unapproved revision's stray page is never validated while bound checks run and amended checks are refused; CL-06 shows a missing rule citation outside Affected is still a defect. A gate that names a missing brief for a new approval, or accepts a mismatched legacy brief, fails these cases. The suite proves only the cases it contains; the wrong-Bound-hash variant is absent (F1).

bun run package:verify regenerates the three distributions and the CLI reference in memory and compares them with the tracked manifest and any built tree (run-3 log: "ok packages (20 files)", "ok cli-reference", exit 0). The manifest diff updates exactly the two edited skills, grace5-prepare and grace5-orchestrate, in all three layouts, while the grace5-execute and grace5-review hashes stay byte-identical because those skills were not edited; the cli-reference diff matches the help-text changes in cli.ts. A stale, missing or extra generated entry, or guidance edited without regeneration, fails verify. The comparison is circular for a systematic generator mistake, since the manifest is written by the generator it verifies; the diff read anchors it outside that loop: the changed hashes correspond one-to-one to the two changed skill sources, and CK8 confirms the retired documents left the tracked tree the packages materialize from.

The capture command reads all seven guidance files (the four skills, method.md, authorization.md, commands.md), fails on any missing or unreadable file because readFileSync throws before the marker, requires "independent contract read" in the prepare skill, and forbids brief-<rev>, "independent brief", "brief writer" and "brief for approval" in each file; the marker "briefless guidance: ok" prints only after every file passes (run-3 log). A pass separates guidance that still instructs the retired page, writer or handoff from guidance that does not, and a prepare skill that dropped the independent read fails outright. The trace is a static text scan: origin=any with device and build absent is honest, no device being involved, and the claim is marker-sequence-unattributed. Its limit is phrasing: a brief instruction worded outside the four patterns would evade the regex; the complete diff read covers that, no skill now containing the word "brief" at all, and the prepare skill carrying the findings-only read with no page, template, writer metadata or fidelity parser.

Review.Rule: K1's surface holds: no command, check kind, receipt field, review rule or approval artifact is added — the approval record is the same artifact with brief-sha256 made optional, and the only lifecycle artifact removed is the brief. The approval rule is rewritten to the contract ("on the contract ... bound to the contract text, its checks and the decision"); the new findings-only independent-contract-read rule is the replacement mechanism the contract's Change and D9 mandate, recorded as L-33 rather than an unrelated addition; and the packages rule is followed, skills/ being edited and bun run package regenerating the tracked manifest (CK4). No release identity moved. The check rule-3 exemption implements the Affected exception commands.md already stated before this change; it adds no surface.

Judged against the current rule file, which this change amends under its own Affected. An approval binds the contract text, each check definition and the decision; brief-sha256 is optional and legacy; the owner approves alone on the contract and no agent infers approval. Removing the brief hash weakens no authority: contract-sha256 and every Bound are still required and checked (check rule 7, the unbound obligation, the BN-01 and unbound tests), and a contract edited after approval is still reported altered and treated as unapproved with no brief to hide it (the altered-contract test; authorizationOf unchanged). C-0019's own approval-1.xml is a legacy record carrying brief-sha256, approved under the pre-retirement kernel; its brief obligation is preserved, not rewritten.

K3 holds. A legacy approval with brief-sha256 still requires its brief to match (state.ts step 2 unchanged for legacy; BN-02, BN-03, FS-12, FS-14, RV-04 and RV-10 retained), a new approval requires none (BN-01), and no historical record is deleted or rewritten: the closed C-0018 records in the diff are the kernel's own close move with bytes preserved, and the example briefs stay tracked (CK8). The supersession table and close steps 1-2 are amended to match the code. The check rule-3 deviation the implementer flagged is judged justified here: closed C-0007 and C-0016 cite models/architecture/brief.md as a rule, so deleting it would make check report a defect on records that must stay readable (A7); the exemption is scoped to the change's own Affected (Path and Protected), matches the exception commands.md already documented, keeps a missing citation outside Affected a defect (CL-06), and is the minimal means to keep CK3's all-closed sweep clean. It weakens no check for open changes beyond the pre-existing documented Affected exception.

L-04 is retired with the owner's stated burden (a brief that duplicates the contract with inflated prose, consumes preparation time and budget, and adds no decision the owner cannot take on the contract) and the removal criterion that was met, matching the original criterion's first clause (no information at pilot sizes, fidelity checking finding no decision that would otherwise be missed); its source, alternative, benefit and cost cells are preserved. L-05 is amended to the contract-only binding with legacy brief-hash acceptance. L-33 records the retirement and the findings-only independent contract read with an explicit owner-requirement source, a smallest alternative, benefit, cost and a removal criterion, as the ledger rule demands for the replacement mechanism; the edits to L-03, L-06, L-16, L-27 and L-29 only strip brief references. No unrelated mechanism is added.

K5 and N4 hold. package.json, .grace5/kernel-version and src/upgrade/ are absent from the diff; the README status line still reads "Version 0.8.0, the last release" with only the surrounding approval prose reworded; no migration boundary or versioned table row is registered. Making brief-sha256 and close/@brief optional is a backward-compatible stored-record schema preparation — legacy records still validate and new records are written only by the new kernel — which upgrade.md permits ordinary changes to prepare; the release registers any boundary it carries. No release act is performed or implied.
